subject: Hosted API pricing — token volume + peak TPS follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@retailco.com>, Emily Zhang <emily@fintech.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — token volume + peak TPS follow-up

Hi Tom / Emily —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together an accurate hosted-API pricing estimate and unit-economics sheet.

Recap from the discovery call:
- Primary use: customer-facing chat + summary generation across retail product pages.
- Model profile: low-latency generation (<= 400ms avg), moderate context (~2k tokens typical).
- Current interest: start with hosted API, may move to Dedicated if peak capacity/latency requires.

Asks for pricing estimate (most important):
1) Expected monthly token volume (approximate is fine) — counts both input+output tokens.
2) Peak TPS (requests per second) during peak minute(s) — or typical concurrency for chat sessions.
3) Target budget range and any internal target $/1M tokens (if you have a preferred economics target).

Attached: Redwood_pricing_walkthrough.pdf (high-level tiers) and a small usage_estimate.csv you can edit if you want to share a day-by-day profile.

If you can send approx. numbers, Sean and I will run unit-economics scenarios (list vs committed) and flag whether Dedicated capacity looks necessary for your peak TPS/latency SLOs.

Thanks —

Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@retailco.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhang <emily@fintech.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — token volume + peak TPS follow-up

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the recap — that matches our notes. Quick answers below. I put Emily on reply since she's helping with the estimates.

1) Expected monthly token volume: approx 300,000,000 tokens/month (includes inputs and outputs). We expect it to ramp over 3 months to this level.
2) Peak TPS: rough peak of ~25 TPS during flash sale events; typical peak concurrency for support/chat is ~10 TPS.
3) Budget: early-stage procurement target is $3k–$6k/month. We don't have an internal $/1M target — open to what makes sense given model choice and SLOs.

We care about predictable per-token unit economics and a fallback plan if latency spikes during promotions. Can you show a few scenarios (list price, committed discount tiers, and whether Dedicated makes sense for the 25 TPS peaks)?

Also, would need sample SLA language and an MSA once we align on the numbers.

Thanks —

Tom Lewis
Head of Product Operations | RetailCo
Tom.Lewis@retailco.com | +1 (212) 555-0123

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@retailco.com>, Emily Zhang <emily@fintech.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — Hosted API unit economics + capacity notes

On Fri, Mar 13, 2026 at 09:42 AM Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@retailco.com> wrote:
> 1) Expected monthly token volume: approx 300,000,000 tokens/month
> 2) Peak TPS: rough peak of ~25 TPS
> 3) Budget: $3k–$6k/month

Tom — thanks for the clarity. A few quick data points and a proposal for next steps: 

Unit-economics (hosted API, ballpark):
- List price (general hosted tier): $12 per 1M tokens.
- Committed volume discount (monthly commit >= 100M): $8 per 1M tokens.
- For 300M tokens/month:
  - List cost = 300 * $12 = $3,600/month.
  - Committed estimate = 300 * $8 = $2,400/month.

Notes on peak TPS and capacity:
- 25 TPS peak for short windows (flash sales) is within hosted multi-tenant capacity for typical generation workloads, but
  if you need strict p95 latency guarantees during those peaks we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) or a hybrid fallback rule (hosted + Dedicated warm standby).
- Dedicated capacity pricing is a separate commit (monthly GPU pool) — we'll scope that if you want hard SLOs for 99th/95th percentiles.

Next steps I propose:
1) Alex: send a short pricing scenarios pdf (list vs commit) showing the math and any upfront commit terms.
2) Tom / Emily: confirm whether 300M is steady-state or peak-month and whether the 25 TPS is sustained >5m or <1m bursts.
3) If committed pricing looks interesting, we can draft a term-sheet + MSA sample.

I'll attach a quick spreadsheet with the calculations (Sean_upload_estimates.csv) — Alex, feel free to combine with your walkthrough.

—Sean Gallagher
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@retailco.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — token volume + peak TPS follow-up

Alex / Sean —

This is helpful, thanks. A couple quick clarifications:
- 300M is our expected steady-state after the three-month ramp.
- The 25 TPS peaks are short bursts (typically 1–3 minutes) during promotions.

We'd like to see the short pricing scenarios (list vs committed) and a recommendation on whether to start on Hosted with a hybrid fallback (warm Dedicated standby) or to go straight to Dedicated for peace-of-mind on SLA.

If you can send a term-sheet + a sample MSA we can run legal review in parallel. Once we have the numbers I'll share them with procurement to confirm the $3k–$6k/month envelope — if committed pricing can get us to the low end of that envelope we're likely to move forward.

I'll look out for the materials Monday.

Thanks,
Tom
